data.narrative:
Aeva Technologies is a publicly traded semiconductor company founded by Soroush Salehian and Mina Rezk, having raised $660M+ and currently valued at $1.09B. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 3 public peers in the Chips & Semiconductors sector (Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and Ouster), supplemented by 8 private frontier-tech comparables including SambaNova Systems and Etched.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Across the 3 same-sector, same-stage public comparables, valuations range from $2.3B (Ouster) to $39.2B (Cerebras), with a median of $35.8B. A public-comp anchoring method using price-to-sales multiples (median 20.4x across ALAB, NVDA, and AMD) cannot be applied due to lack of disclosed revenue data for Aeva. This is a structural constraint typical of private-stage analysis, even for recently public entities with limited disclosure.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $30.4B to $41.2B, centered on the peer median of $35.8B. Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion within the peer set (nearly 17x between Ouster and Cerebras), which reflects heterogeneity in revenue scale, profitability, and market positioning across semiconductor competitors. Revenue visibility and near-term path to positive unit economics remain critical variables not captured by comparables alone. The single-method triangulation limits conviction; incorporation of revenue or margin multiples would narrow this range substantially.
